correctness.rationale: PASS. A normal contact of a generic interior point with a strictly convex polygon is an interior side-foot minimum or a vertex maximum of squared distance along the polygon boundary; no vertex interior-point local minimum is possible. Alternation gives N=2S. For opposite parallel sides, the orthogonal-foot intervals are identical precisely when their endpoints have equal Euclidean radii. In a cyclic central hexagon all opposite-side feet activate together; S is twice the sum of three strip indicators, so N is one of 4,8,12. The 12-half-plane clipping formula exactly computes nu=Pr(N=12). Hug's known average-normal n(P)=8 for cyclic centrally symmetric polygons implies Pr4=Pr12=nu. Conversely an obtuse noncyclic hexagon has an unmatched threshold endpoint line entering a nonempty interior segment, across which S changes by one and N by two, forcing a positive-area mod4 violation. Independently clipped regular and arc-gap (pi/2,pi/4,pi/4) examples and obtained area ratios 1/3 and 8sqrt(2)-11 to <1e-12 absolute error. Boundary exceptional lines are measure zero; no noncyclic law claimed.
residual_risks: Independently repeated finite computations do not substitute for universal arguments, which were separately reconstructed where applicable.
